name: New homes completed
definition: Net change in Class A (permanent) housing units from completed new buildings, alterations and demolitions in New York City, by calendar year of completion.

latest_extra.note: Partial year: net units completed in 2026 so far in Housing Database release 26q2.1 (DCP's quarterly release naming; this release runs through the second quarter of 2026). Not comparable with full-year totals.

source.name: NYC Department of City Planning, Housing Database, Community District summary (release 26q2.1), NYC Open Data dbdt-5s7j

peers.note: Different measure from the New York series: these are housing units authorized by building permits in 2025 per 1,000 residents (Census Bureau Building Permits Survey, annual place file; permit-issuing places matched on state and FIPS place code, summing every county part; New York City is the sum of its five borough rows), not net units completed. Permits lead completions by a year or more and are gross, not net of demolitions. Population: Census Vintage 2025 city estimates from data/peers.json. New York City: 19763 units permitted in 2025. Indianapolis: BPS reports the consolidated city (FIPS 36000), divided here by the population of the balance (36003), so its rate is slightly overstated. No row of its own in the BPS place file, so left out: Charlotte.

source.name: U.S. Census Bureau, Building Permits Survey, annual place-level files, 2025 (ne/mw/so/we2025a.txt)

method: Summed the compYYYY columns (net Class A units completed in that calendar year) over all 71 community-district rows of DCP's Housing Database summary table, including joint interest areas, so the total covers the whole city. 2010 uses the full-year column comp2010, not comp2010ap (April 1 to December 31). Borough = first digit of the community district code.
caveats: Net figure: units added by new buildings and alterations minus units removed by demolitions and alterations.
DCP counts units as completed when the Department of Buildings issues a certificate of occupancy, so recent years can be revised upward in later releases as certificates are recorded.
Counts only Class A (permanent) units in jobs filed with the Department of Buildings since 2010; it excludes hotels, dormitories and other Class B units.
The 2026 figure is a partial year and is shown only as a latest reading.
